lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mark where you would pause in a short fable tell and why.

FEEDBACK
Pause before the moral (and lightly at the problem) so the lesson can land.

CHECK
Racing past the ending hides the moral.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Tell your fable in under 90 seconds. Note one pause choice and one listener comment about the moral.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Tell your fable in under 90 seconds. Note one pause choice and one listener comment about the moral. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Pause before the moral (and lightly at the problem) so the lesson can land. Reasoning: I used tell by attending to fable rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Racing past the ending hides the moral. Correction: Pause before the moral (and lightly at the problem) so the lesson can land. Why: the correction restores accurate use of tell.

Parent: Likely misconception: Racing past the ending hides the moral. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating tell on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with tell, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.
